name: xAI
intro: xAI's standalone AI business — Grok subscriptions plus the API — reached roughly $500M in annualized revenue by mid-2026, up from ~$350M in 2025, with a stated target of $2B for the year. modelTitle: How SuperGrok Tiers Stack From $30 to $300.
modelParagraphs: xAI monetizes two ways. Consumer subscriptions run from free to SuperGrok at $30/month, SuperGrok Plus at $100/month and SuperGrok Heavy at $300/month, distributed through the X app. The API is usage-based: flagship Grok models price around $2.00 per million input tokens and $6.00 per million output tokens, with smaller models at roughly $1.25/$2.50.

The revenue-definition question matters more for xAI than any other lab: reported figures range from ~$350M (Grok product business, 2025) to ~$1B (internally discussed run rate including related-entity deals) to ~$3.8B (Sacra's end-2025 estimate counting X/Tesla-adjacent arrangements). This page uses the conservative standalone basis — Grok subscriptions plus API only, excluding X advertising — which reached ~$500M by mid-2026.

faqs.a: xAI's standalone AI business — Grok subscriptions plus the API — generated roughly $500 million in annualized revenue by mid-2026, up from ~$350M in 2025. The company has reportedly targeted ~$2B for 2026. Figures here exclude X advertising revenue.

faqs.q: Why Do Reported xAI Revenue Numbers Vary So Much?
faqs.a: Because the perimeter varies. The Grok product business alone made ~$350M in 2025; an internally discussed ~$1B run rate included X-adjacent deals; and Sacra's ~$3.8B end-2025 estimate counted arrangements with Elon Musk-affiliated companies. This page uses the conservative standalone basis.

Consumer Grok subscriptions from free to $300/month (SuperGrok Heavy) and usage-based API pricing of roughly $2.00/$6.00 per million input/output tokens on flagship models, with cheaper smaller models below that.

faqs.q: What Is xAI's Valuation and How Much Has It Raised?
faqs.a: A $20 billion raise in January 2026 came at a reported ~$230 billion valuation (pre-merger), bringing total raised above $40 billion including compute-linked structures. The xAI–X merger complicates standalone comparisons.
No. Press reports put burn at $1 billion or more per year against ~$500M of standalone ARR, with heavy GPU and data-center spend the dominant cost.
